"If one perceives a non-human as a non-human and receives food from that being and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk perceives an almsgiver as an almsgiver, receives alms-food from that person, and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives an almsgiver as not an almsgiver, receives food, and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If one perceives one who is not an almsgiver as an almsgiver, receives food, and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If one perceives one who is not an almsgiver as not an almsgiver, receives food, and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if food is received when it is offered with the hand and eaten when it is offered with the hand, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If food is received when it is offered with the hand and eaten when offered without the hand, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If food is received when offered without the hand and eaten when offered with the hand, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If food is received when offered without the hand and eaten when offered without the hand, what is the consequence?"

"There is no offense."

"Venerable one, if a monk receives alms-food from a relative and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"There is no offense."

"Venerable one, if a monk receives and eats not alms-food but other things such as prepared food, beverages, soft foods, or things to be licked, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if alms-food is received before full ordination and eaten before full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If it is received before full ordination and eaten at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If it is received before full ordination and eaten after full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If it is received at the moment of full ordination and eaten at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If it is received at the moment of full ordination and eaten after full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If it is received after full ordination and eaten after full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If it is received after full ordination and eaten before full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk directs a layperson to seek alms-food and then eats it himself, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

Likewise, all of the following cases are wrongdoings: eating food received from a hermaphrodite; from one who has disrobed a nun by force; from one who has killed his father; from one who has killed his mother; from one who has killed an arhat; from one who with malicious intent has drawn blood from a Tathāgata; from one who has gone over to the non-Buddhists; from one who lives as a thief; from one who is dwelling alone; from one who is not a resident; from one in whom a prior offense has arisen; from one who was previously involved in a dispute; from one who has taken a side in a dispute; from one who has surrendered the training; and from food received from a fully ordained nun, a probationer nun, a novice nun, or male novices — all such cases are wrongdoings.

"Venerable one, if one who has surrendered the training receives alms-food and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a nun receives alms-food and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is to be confessed."

"Venerable one, if a probationer nun, a novice nun, or a male novice receives alms-food and eats it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

The detailed explanation of the transgression of drinking water containing living creatures should be set forth in full.

In brief:

Secluded places, and spells of the sky,
The night, the fourth case, hermaphrodites,
Female hermaphrodites, attendants,
Young women, and wandering ascetics.

This was asked of the Blessed One, the Buddha, by the Venerable Upāli.

"Venerable one, if the Blessed One has declared that a monk who forcibly enters a village containing a dangerous woman while seeking alms commits a transgression, then if a monk, while seeking alms, perceives a deserted village containing a dangerous woman as deserted and forcibly enters it, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk, while seeking alms, forcibly enters a village containing a dangerous woman through the sky, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk, while seeking alms, renders himself invisible by means of a mantra or a medicine and enters a village containing a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk, while forcibly entering a village containing a dangerous woman, undergoes a change of sex and becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a nun, while forcibly entering a village containing a dangerous woman, undergoes a change of sex and becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk forcibly enters a village perceiving a human being as a human being, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a human being as not a human being and forcibly enters, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If he perceives a non-human being as a human being and forcibly enters, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If he perceives a non-human being as a non-human being and forcibly enters, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk perceives a dangerous woman as a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a dangerous woman as not a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"There is no offence."

"If he perceives one who is not a dangerous woman as a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"If he perceives one who is not a dangerous woman as not a dangerous woman, there is no offence."

"Venerable one, if a monk, while seeking alms, forcibly enters a hermaphrodite's village that contains a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk forcibly enters together with a hermaphrodite, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk forcibly enters a village containing a dangerous woman seeking refuge, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if monks forcibly approach a young bride, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable one, if a monk, while seeking alms, enters and forcibly stays in the vicinity of a village containing a dangerous woman to the extent of merely hearing distance, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

In brief:

The mad, the mentally disturbed,
The deaf, the dull-witted, the drowsy,
Those in pain, the intoxicated,
Those in absorption, and travelers to other places — these are the final cases.

"Venerable one, if a monk forcibly enters a village of the mad, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrongdoing."

Likewise, forcibly sitting together with the mentally disturbed, those afflicted by illness, the dull-witted, the mute, the deaf, the drowsy, those in pain, the intoxicated, those in meditative absorption, and those dwelling elsewhere — all of these are wrongdoings.

"Venerable one, if one who has been given the training, while seeking alms, forcibly enters a village containing a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a nun, while seeking alms, forcibly enters a village containing a dangerous woman, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

As set forth in the chapter on a probationer nun, a novice nun, or a male novice sitting in concealment in a place containing a dangerous woman, the case of sitting concealed in a place containing a dangerous woman is also to be stated.

In brief:

Messages, letters, hand-signals, and —

"— another's word, and passing from one to another, a madman, one whose mind is disturbed, one who is afflicted, a fool, one who is asleep, one who is intoxicated with alcohol, one who is inebriated, one who has entered meditative absorption, one who has gone elsewhere — these are the final cases."

The venerable Upāli then asked the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable one, the Blessed One has declared that if a monk gives food and drink with his own hand to one who is naked — whether a naked man or naked woman, a male wanderer or female wanderer — it is a transgression. Venerable one, if a monk, through a messenger, gives food and drink with his own hand to one who is naked — whether a naked man or naked woman, a male wanderer or female wanderer — what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If he gives it likewise through a written message, a hand-signal, another's word, or passing it from one to another, what is the consequence in each case?"

"All of these are transgressions."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink with his own hand to a madman who is naked — whether a naked man or naked woman, a male wanderer or female wanderer — what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, one whose mind is disturbed, one tormented by illness, a fool, a mute, one who is afflicted, one who is asleep, one who is intoxicated with alcohol, one who is inebriated, one who has entered meditative absorption, and one who dwells elsewhere — if a monk gives food and drink, whether to a naked man or naked woman, a male wanderer or female wanderer, among all such persons, what is the consequence in each case?"

"All of these are transgressions."

In brief:

Improper food and the naked,
vessels and characteristics, the seventh,
the fourth, mantras (Skt. mantra),
and through another — another's non-Buddhist renunciant.

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink to one who is naked or to a wanderer, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives to such a person, apart from food, other things to eat or drink, to taste, or to lick and so forth, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink with his own hand to ascetics (Skt. śramaṇa) and brahmins other than the naked and the wanderers, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, are there cases in which a monk gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer and yet incurs no fault?"

"Upāli, there are. These are: placing the vessel on the ground and pouring into it before giving; wishing to be free from an evil view held by that person; and giving to a relative."

"Venerable one, if a monk is in the act of giving food and drink with his own hand to one who is naked or a wanderer, and in the course of that act his status changes and he becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a nun is in the act of giving food and drink with her own hand to one who is naked or a wanderer, and in the course of that act her status changes and she becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if one who has not yet received full ordination dedicates food and drink with her own hand to one who is naked or a wanderer, and then gives it before receiving full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one dedicates it before full ordination and gives it at the very moment of receiving full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one dedicates it before full ordination and gives it after having received full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one dedicates it at the very moment of receiving full ordination and gives it at that same moment, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one dedicates it at the very moment of receiving full ordination and gives it after having received full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one who has fully received ordination dedicates it and gives it after having fully received ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one who has fully received ordination dedicates it and gives it before full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk, perceiving a human as human, gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives that human as not human, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives a non-human as human, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives a non-human as non-human, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk makes himself invisible by means of a mantra or medicine, and then gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer, receiving it from another, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer on behalf of another, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer who is a hermaphrodite, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer who is a female hermaphrodite, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if one who has given the precepts gives food and drink to one who is naked or a wanderer, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable one, if a fully ordained nun gives food and drink from her own hand to one who is naked or a wanderer, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable one, if a female probationer, a novice nun, or a male novice gives food and drink from their own hand to one who is naked or a wanderer, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

In brief:

The mad one and the mentally disturbed,
the deaf, the wanderers, and their kinds,
the king who holds the seventh view,
the fourth ones, and the hermaphrodites.

The venerable Upāli asked the Blessed One, the buddha: "Venerable one, the Blessed One has declared that whatever monk goes to watch a battle array incurs a downfall. If a monk goes to watch a battle array where there are mad combatants, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if those who are mentally disturbed, afflicted by illness, dull-witted, mute, or deaf go to watch a battle array in the same way, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk goes to watch a battle array that is stationed in another region, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if, while a monk is going to watch a battle array, he undergoes a change of marks and becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable one, if, while a nun is going to watch a battle array, she undergoes a change of marks and becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable one, if a monk, when looking at a battle array, goes only as far as the surrounding area, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, is there a case in which a monk may go to watch a battle array without incurring an offense?"
"Upāli, there is: namely, when a monk has been summoned by a royal messenger."

"Venerable one, if one who has not received full ordination goes there in body, and while not yet fully ordained looks on, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one who has not received full ordination goes there and looks on at the time of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one who has not received full ordination goes there and looks on after full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one who is at the time of receiving full ordination goes there and looks on at the time of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one who is at the time of receiving full ordination goes there and looks on after full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one who has fully received ordination goes there and looks on while fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one who has fully received ordination goes there and looks on before full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk perceives a human battle array as a human battle array and goes to watch it, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one perceives a human battle array as a non-human battle array, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives a non-human battle array as a human battle array, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives a non-human battle array as a non-human battle array, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk goes to watch a battle array of neither-male-nor-female beings, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if one who has been given a training rule goes to watch a battle array, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable one, if a fully ordained nun goes to watch a battle array, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable one, if female probationers, female novices, and male novices go to watch a battle array, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

As for watching a battle array — in the same way as the chapter on the training rules, all the cases of staying no more than two nights should be stated in full.

In brief:

By message, by letter, by gesture,
by having another say it, or relayed from one to the next;
one who is insane, one whose mind is disturbed, one who is ill,
one who is deaf, one who is foolish, one who is asleep,
one who is delirious, one who is intoxicated,
one who has entered meditative absorption — these are the last.

The venerable Upāli asked the buddha, the Blessed One: "Venerable one, the Blessed One has said that whatever monk strikes a monk incurs a downfall. Venerable one, if a monk sends a strike to a monk by message, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if one causes a strike to be delivered by letter, by gesture, by having another say it, or relayed from one to the next — all of these are transgressions."

"Venerable one, if a monk strikes a monk who is insane, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if one strikes a monk whose mind is disturbed, one afflicted by illness, one who is deaf, one who is asleep, one who is delirious, one who is intoxicated, one who has entered meditative absorption, or — in the same manner — a monk who abides elsewhere in another destiny: all of these are transgressions."

In brief:

By mantra, by medicine, by another's means,
the fourth and seventh done by another,
householders and those like them,
by night likewise, and a fully ordained nun.

"Venerable one, if a monk renders himself invisible by means of a mantra or medicine and then strikes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, is there a case where one strikes a monk and yet the fault does not become a downfall?"
"Upāli, there is: if one strikes thinking it to be play, or if one strikes thinking it to be accidental."

"Venerable one, if a monk strikes a monk on behalf of another, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk causes another to be struck, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk perceives a human as a human and strikes, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one perceives a human as a non-human, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives a non-human as a human, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives a non-human as a non-human, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a monk perceives one who is fully ordained as fully ordained and strikes, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one perceives one who is fully ordained as not fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives one who is not fully ordained as fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one perceives one who is not fully ordained as not fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if one prepares to strike before full ordination has been received and then strikes before full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one prepares to strike before full ordination and then strikes at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one prepares to strike before full ordination and then strikes after full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one prepares to strike at the moment of full ordination and then strikes at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one prepares to strike at the moment of full ordination and then strikes after full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one prepares to strike after full ordination has been received and then strikes after full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one prepares to strike after full ordination has been received and then strikes before full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk strikes a layman, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Similarly, if one strikes a woman, a eunuch, a nun who has been expelled, one who has killed his father, one who has killed his mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who has maliciously shed the blood of a Tathāgata, a tīrthika, one who has gone over to the tīrthikas, one who dwells as a thief, one who does not dwell in the community, one who dwells separately, one against whom an earlier offense has arisen, or one with whom there has been an earlier dispute — in all such cases it is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk strikes one who has caused a schism in the Saṅgha, one who has sided with the schism, or one who has been given a formal act of instruction — what is the consequence in all such cases?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable ones, if a monk is striking another monk and that other's sex changes so that he becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a nun is striking another nun and that other's sex changes so that she becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk strikes a nun, a probationer, a female novice, or a male novice, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a nun strikes a monk, a probationer, a female novice, or a male novice, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if one who has been given a formal act of instruction strikes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable ones, if a nun strikes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If she strikes a probationer, a female novice, or a male novice, it is a transgression."

Just as the chapter on striking has been set forth, so too the chapter on threatening to strike is to be stated in the same way.

In brief:
By message, letter, or gesture,
by having another say it, or by passing word from one to another —
if one is mad, mentally disturbed, or afflicted by illness,
or is mute, deaf, or asleep,
or is in delirium, drunk,
in meditative absorption, or gone elsewhere — these are the last cases.

The venerable Upāli asked the buddha, the Blessed One: "Venerable one, the Blessed One has said that whichever monk confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense is guilty of a downfall. If a monk confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense by means of a messenger, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if such a charge is conveyed by letter, by gesture, by having another say it, or by passing it from one to another — in all such cases it is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense by conveying it through a madman, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if conveyed through one who is mentally disturbed, one afflicted by illness, one who is simple-minded, one who is mute, one who is deaf, one who is asleep, one in delirium, one who is drunk, one in meditative absorption, or one who has gone to dwell elsewhere — in all such cases it is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts a monk who is mad with a charge of a grave offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, monks who are mentally disturbed, afflicted by illness, simple-minded, mute, deaf, asleep, delirious, drunk, in meditative absorption, or dwelling elsewhere — if a monk confronts such monks with a charge of a grave offense, in all such cases it is a transgression."

In brief:
By voice, by body, by solitude,
by the fourth and seventh offense categories,
against laymen and the rest —
such is the confronting with charges, and so too for nuns.

"Venerable ones, if a monk, having been questioned, confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense in the noble language, and that monk does not acknowledge it in the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If someone from the borderlands confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense in the borderlands language, and that monk does not acknowledge it in the borderlands language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If someone from the borderlands confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense in the borderlands language—"

"—and that monk does not acknowledge it in the borderlands language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If someone from the borderlands confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense in the noble language, and that monk does not acknowledge it in the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk, having been questioned, confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense by means of a physical gesture, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, is there a case in which a monk confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense, and yet it does not constitute an offense?"
"Upāli, there is. It is when, on account of that charge, a monk's livelihood is disrupted, his life as a renunciant is disrupted, or his practice of the holy life is disrupted."

"Venerable ones, is there a case in which a monk confronts a monk with a charge, and yet it does not constitute a downfall?"
"Upāli, there is. It is when he confronts him with a charge of an offense other than a grave offense."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts a monk with a charge of a grave offense, and then a change of status occurs so that the monk becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a nun confronts a nun with a charge of a grave offense, and then a change of status occurs so that the nun becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk perceives a grave offense as a grave offense and confronts the monk with a charge accordingly, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If he perceives a grave offense as not a grave offense and confronts him with a charge, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives something that is not a grave offense as not a grave offense and confronts him with a charge, what is the consequence?"
"There is no offense."

"If he perceives something that is not a grave offense as a grave offense and confronts him with a charge, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk perceives a fully ordained person as fully ordained and confronts him with a charge of a grave offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If he perceives a fully ordained person as not fully ordained and confronts the monk with a charge of a grave offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a person who is not fully ordained as not fully ordained and confronts him with a charge, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a person who is not fully ordained as fully ordained and confronts him with a charge, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if, at the time of full ordination, one sees a grave offense by a monk and then confronts him with a charge when he is not yet fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one sees it at a time when he is not yet fully ordained and confronts him with a charge when the ordination is in progress, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one sees it at a time when he is not yet fully ordained and confronts him with a charge when he is fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one sees it when the ordination is in progress and confronts him with a charge while the ordination is in progress, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one sees it when the ordination is in progress and confronts him with a charge after ordination is complete, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one sees it at the time of full ordination and confronts him with a charge at the time of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one sees it at the time of full ordination and confronts him with a charge when he is not yet fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts a layman with a charge of a grave offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

Likewise, if one confronts any of the following with a charge of a grave offense — a eunuch, a hermaphrodite, a suspended nun, one who has killed his father, one who has killed his mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who with malicious intent has drawn blood from a Tathāgata, a robber who has remained in the order, one who has not remained in the order, one who dwells apart, a non-Buddhist adherent, one who has gone over to non-Buddhist adherents, one who previously caused a schism, or one against whom a prior offense has arisen — in all such cases it constitutes a transgression.

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts with a charge of a grave offense those who have caused a schism in the Saṅgha, those who have sided with them, or those to whom a rule of training has been administered, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts a layperson with a charge of a grave monastic offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if he confronts any of them — from a female trainee down to one against whom a prior offense has arisen — in all such cases it is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts those who have caused a schism in the Saṅgha, those who have sided with them, or those to whom a rule of training has been administered with a charge of a grave monastic offense, what is the consequence?"
"In every case it is a downfall."

"Venerable ones, if a monk speaks of a grave monastic offense to a layperson, does that count as having formally confronted him with it?"
"Upāli, it does not."

"Likewise, if he speaks of it to any of them — from a female trainee down to one to whom a rule of training has been administered — does that count as having formally confronted them?"
"Upāli, it does not."

"Venerable ones, if a monk confronts a fully ordained nun, a female trainee, a female novice, or a male novice with a charge of a grave monastic offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a fully ordained nun confronts a monk, a female trainee, a female novice, or a male novice with a charge of a grave monastic offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if one to whom a rule of training has been administered confronts another with a charge of a grave monastic offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable ones, if a fully ordained nun confronts another fully ordained nun with a charge of a grave monastic offense, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"And if she confronts a female trainee, a female novice, or a male novice with such a charge, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

This is the noble Vinaya, the eleventh fascicle.

In summary:

By message, by letter, by gesture,
through another's words, or relayed from one to the next,
through madness, mental disturbance, illness,
deafness, dullness, sleep,
incoherence, intoxication,
and one in meditative absorption going elsewhere — these are the last.

The venerable Upāli addressed the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable Blessed One, you have declared that if a monk says to another monk, intending to have him separated from his food, 'Venerable, whether you speak with me or keep my company, things will not go well for you — you should leave,' and thereby causes that monk to be separated from his food even for a single moment, it becomes a downfall. Now, venerable one, if a monk causes another monk to be separated from his food by a personal message, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if it is done by a written letter, by a gesture, through another's words, or relayed from one to the next and he is thereby separated from his food, in all such cases it is a transgression."

"Venerable ones, if a monk causes a mad monk to be separated from his food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if he causes any of the following to be separated from their food — one whose mind is disturbed, one tormented by illness, one who is mute, one who is deaf, one who is dull-witted, one who is asleep, one who is incoherent, one who is intoxicated, one who has entered meditative absorption, or a monk who is residing elsewhere — in all such cases it is a transgression."

In summary:

By voice, by body, in private,
by one using another's name,
laypersons and so forth —
the fourth and seventh concern food.

"Venerable ones, if a noble monk separates another monk from food using the noble language, and that monk does not understand the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk separates another from food using a regional border language, and that monk does not understand the regional border language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one from the border regions separates another from food using a border language, and that monk does not understand the border language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one from the border regions separates another from food using the noble language, and that monk does not understand the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk separates another monk from food using a physical gesture as the indicator, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk perceives a secluded place as not secluded and separates another from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk instructs another to separate someone else from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk separates another from food on behalf of a third party, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk is in the process of separating another monk from food, and in the course of that act the monk changes gender and becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble nun is in the process of separating another nun from food, and in the course of that act the nun changes gender and becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk separates a layman from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

Likewise, in all the following cases — separating a laywoman from food, separating an intersex person from food, separating one who has been expelled from the nuns' order, separating one who has killed a father, one who has killed a mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who has drawn blood from a Tathāgata with malicious intent, a non-Buddhist adherent (tīrthika), one who has gone over to the non-Buddhists, one who has taken up a life of theft, one who is not residing in the community, one who is residing separately, one against whom an offence was previously committed, and one with whom a dispute previously arose — in all such cases the consequence is a transgression.

"If a noble monk separates from food one who has schismed the Saṅgha, one who has sided with a schism, or one who has given training rules, what is the consequence?"
"In every case it is a downfall."

"If a noble monk perceives a human being as a human being and separates that person from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a monk perceives a human being as not a human being and separates that person from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives a non-human being as not a human being and separates that being from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives a non-human being as a human being and separates that being from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk perceives one who is fully ordained as fully ordained and separates that person from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a monk perceives one who is fully ordained as not fully ordained and separates that person from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives one who is not fully ordained as fully ordained and separates that person from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives one who is not fully ordained as not fully ordained and separates that person from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Noble one, if a monk who is not yet fully ordained invites a guest, and that guest is also not yet fully ordained at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk who is not yet fully ordained invites a guest, and that guest has since received full ordination at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk who is not yet fully ordained invites a guest, and that guest is in the very act of receiving full ordination at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk who is in the very act of receiving full ordination invites a guest, and that guest is also in the very act of receiving full ordination at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk who is in the very act of receiving full ordination invites a guest, and that guest has already received full ordination at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk who is fully ordained invites a guest, and that guest is also fully ordained at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a monk who is fully ordained invites a guest, and that guest is not yet fully ordained at the time of being separated from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Noble one, are there cases in which a monk separates another monk from food and yet incurs no offence or downfall?"
"Upāli, there are. It is the case of one who is separated from food on the prescription of a physician."

"Noble one, are there cases in which a monk is separated from food and yet it does not constitute a downfall?"
"Upāli, there are. If, apart from food proper, one is separated from other kinds of provisions — namely things to be eaten, things to be drunk, things to be tasted, things to be licked, and the like — the consequence is a transgression, not a downfall."

"If a noble monk separates a nun, a female probationer, a female novice, or male novices from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble nun separates a monk, a female probationer, a female novice, or male novices from food, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk, applying a precept, separates a fully ordained monk from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a noble nun separates a fully ordained nun from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a female probationer, a female novice, or male novices separate a fully ordained monk, a fully ordained nun, a female probationer, a female novice, or male novices from food, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

In summary:
By messenger, by letter, by gesture,
by having another convey it, from one to another,
whether one has become mad, is mentally disturbed,
is ill, is disabled, or is traveling.

Venerable Upāli then asked the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable one, if the Blessed One has declared that whichever monk, without having requested permission, causes another to enter or exit a fire on his own behalf, incurs a downfall — if a monk causes another to enter or exit by means of a messenger, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"Likewise, if he causes another to enter or exit a fire by means of a letter, by gesture, by having another convey it, or by passing it from one to another, all such cases are transgressions."

"If a noble monk causes a madman to enter or exit a fire, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"Likewise, if he causes someone mentally disturbed, someone tormented by illness, a simpleton, a mute, a disabled person, or one who has gone to dwell in another place to enter or exit — all such cases are transgressions."

In summary:
By voice, by body, by a secluded place,
and in the same manner one reveals another's marks to others —
whether to householders and the like:
the fourth and seventh rules are the same.

"If a noble monk causes someone to enter or exit using the noble language, and that monk does not know the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a noble one causes someone to enter or exit using a border language, and that monk does not know the border language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a border person causes someone to enter or exit using a border language, and that monk does not know the border language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a border person causes someone to enter or exit using the noble language, and that monk does not know the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk causes someone to enter or exit by means of a physical gesture, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk, perceiving a place of solitude as not being solitary, causes someone to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk causes another person to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a noble monk causes someone to enter or exit on behalf of another person, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If, while a noble monk is causing someone to enter or exit, that person's gender changes and he becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If, while a noble nun is causing someone to enter or exit, that person's gender changes and she becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a noble monk causes a householder who is visibly present to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."
"Likewise, if he causes a eunuch, a hermaphrodite, a nun who has been expelled, one who has killed his father, one who has killed his mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who with malicious intent has drawn blood from a Tathāgata, a non-Buddhist adherent, one who has gone over to the non-Buddhists, one who has remained among thieves, one who has previously caused strife, or one against whom a previous offense has arisen, to enter or exit — in all such cases it is a downfall."

"If a noble monk causes those who have schismatized the Saṅgha, those who have sided with schismatics, or those upon whom a disciplinary measure has been imposed to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"In all such cases it is a downfall."

"If a noble monk, perceiving a human being as a human being, causes that person to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."
"If he perceives a human being as not a human being and causes that person to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he perceives a non-human being as a human being and causes that person to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he perceives a non-human being as a non-human being and causes that person to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a noble monk, when a person has not yet received full ordination, arranges for a candidate who has not yet received full ordination, and causes that person to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he arranges for a candidate who has not yet received full ordination, and causes someone who is in the process of receiving full ordination to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he arranges for a candidate who has not yet received full ordination, and causes someone who has fully received ordination to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he arranges for someone who is in the process of receiving full ordination, and causes someone who is in the process of receiving full ordination to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he arranges for someone who is in the process of receiving full ordination, and causes someone who has fully received ordination to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If he arranges for someone who has fully received ordination, and causes someone who has fully received ordination to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."
"If he arranges for someone who has fully received ordination, and causes someone who has not yet received full ordination to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a noble monk causes someone to enter or exit by means of giving a training precept, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."
"If a noble monk causes this through a fully ordained nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."
"If probationary nuns, novice nuns, or male novices cause someone to enter or exit, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

In brief:

By message, by letter, by gesture,
through another's words, or passed along from one to the next,
through a madman, one mentally disturbed, one who is ill,
one who is mute, one who is an idiot, one who is asleep,
one who is about to sneeze, one who is intoxicated,
and one who has entered meditative absorption — these are the last cases.

The venerable Upāli asked the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable one, the Blessed One taught that if a monk, having received a gift of faith for a deed in conformity with the Dharma of the Saṅgha, thereafter performs a deed of entanglement with respect to that same matter, and then says, 'Monk, I will not give you the gift of faith — relinquish it!' — he incurs a downfall." The venerable one then asked: "If a monk, having received a gift of faith for a deed in conformity with the Dharma of the Saṅgha, thereafter performs a deed of entanglement through a message, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"Likewise, if he performs a deed of entanglement through a letter, through a gesture, through another's words, or by passing it along from one to the next, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a monk, having received a gift of faith for a deed in conformity with the Dharma of the Saṅgha, thereafter performs a deed of entanglement with respect to a madman, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"Likewise, if the deed of entanglement is performed with respect to one who is mentally disturbed, one afflicted by illness, one who is mute, one who is an idiot, one who is deaf, one who is asleep, one about to sneeze, one who is intoxicated, one who has entered meditative absorption, or one who is dwelling elsewhere — in all such cases it is a transgression."

In brief:

By voice, by body, by solitude,
likewise, by one person indicating another's mark,
with respect to householders and others of that kind —
the fourth and seventh cases are likewise so.

"If a noble monk performs a deed of entanglement with a monk using the refined language of the noble ones, and that monk does not understand the refined language of the noble ones, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a noble one performs a deed of entanglement with a monk using the language of the borderlands, and that monk does not understand the language of the borderlands, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a borderlander performs a deed of entanglement with a monk using the language of the borderlands, and that monk does not understand the language of the borderlands, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a borderlander performs a deed of entanglement with a monk using the refined language of the noble ones, and that monk does not understand the refined language of the noble ones, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a monk performs a deed of entanglement by means of a bodily sign, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a monk performs a deed of entanglement perceiving a secluded place as non-secluded, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a monk instructs another to perform a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a monk performs a deed of entanglement on behalf of another, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a monk, while performing a deed of entanglement, changes his status and becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."
"If a nun, while performing a deed of entanglement, changes her status and becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If a monk performs a deed of entanglement with a layman, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

Likewise, if a deed of entanglement is performed with a hermaphrodite, with a paṇḍaka, with an expelled nun, with one who has killed his father, with one who has killed his mother, with one who has killed an arhat, with one who has drawn blood from a Tathāgata with malicious intent, with a non-Buddhist adherent (tīrthika), with one who has gone over to the non-Buddhist adherents, with one who is dwelling as a thief, with one who is not dwelling in proper standing, with one who is dwelling apart, with one against whom a prior offence has arisen, or with one involved in a prior dispute — in all such cases it becomes a transgression.

"If a monk performs a deed of entanglement with one who has caused a schism in the Saṅgha, with one who has sided with that schism, or with one who has been given a training — what is the consequence?"
"In every case it becomes a downfall."

"If a monk perceives a Dharma-conformant act as a Dharma-conformant act and, granting consent, performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a monk perceives a Dharma-conformant act as one that is not Dharma-conformant and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives a non-Dharma-conformant act as a Dharma-conformant act and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives a non-Dharma-conformant act as a non-Dharma-conformant act and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives one who has received full ordination as one who has received full ordination and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a monk perceives one who has received full ordination as one who has not received full ordination and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives one who has not received full ordination as one who has received full ordination and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk perceives one who has not received full ordination as one who has not received full ordination and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If consent is given during the period before full ordination and a deed of entanglement is performed during that same pre-ordination period, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If consent is given during the period before full ordination and a deed of entanglement is performed at the very moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If consent is given during the period before full ordination and a deed of entanglement is performed after full ordination has been received, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If consent is given at the very moment of full ordination and a deed of entanglement is performed at that same moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If consent is given at the very moment of full ordination and a deed of entanglement is performed after full ordination has been completed, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If consent is given after full ordination has been completed and a deed of entanglement is performed by one who has completed full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If consent is given at the time of full ordination and a deed of entanglement is performed in the pre-ordination period, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a monk grants consent to a Dharma-conformant act of the Saṅgha and then performs a deed of entanglement with a nun, a probationer nun (śikṣamāṇā), a female novice, or male novices, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If a nun performs a deed of entanglement with a monk, a probationer nun, a female novice, or male novices, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If one who has been given a training grants consent to a Dharma-conformant act of the Saṅgha and performs a deed of entanglement, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a monk performs a deed of entanglement apart from having granted consent to a Dharma-conformant act of the Saṅgha, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"For a nun, a probationer nun, a female novice, and male novices, it becomes a transgression."

In brief:
One who has become mad, or whose mind is disturbed,
one who is sick, or one who walks while casting a spell,
at the middle watch of the night and at the fourth watch,
likewise an emanation, a paṇḍaka,
one who is veiled, one who is surrounded, and a nun —

The venerable Upāli asked the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable Blessed One, you have declared that if a monk sleeps in the same dwelling together with an unordained person for more than two nights, it becomes a downfall. Venerable One, if a monk sleeps together with a mad person in a dwelling for two nights, and then on the third night sleeps together with one who is in their natural state of mind, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable One, if a monk sleeps for two nights with one who is in their natural state of mind, and then on the third night sleeps together with a mad person, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Likewise, if he sleeps together with one whose mind is disturbed, one tormented by illness, a deaf person, a mute, or one who dwells in another place of existence — all of these become transgressions."

"Venerable One, if a monk, having made himself invisible through a spell or medicine, sleeps in the same dwelling together with an unordained person for more than two nights, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable One, if a monk sleeps in the open sky together with an unordained person for more than two nights, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable One, if a monk sleeps with an unordained person for two nights in the same dwelling, and then on the third night sleeps together with a woman, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk perceives an unordained person as unordained and sleeps with that person for more than two nights, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If he perceives an unordained person as fully ordained and sleeps with that person, what is the consequence?"
"There is no offense."

"If he perceives a fully ordained person as unordained and sleeps with that person, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a fully ordained person as fully ordained and sleeps with that person, what is the consequence?"
"There is no offense."

"Venerable One, if a monk perceives a human as human and sleeps for more than two nights with that person, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If he perceives a human as a non-human and sleeps with that being, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a non-human as human and sleeps with that being, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"If he perceives a non-human as a non-human and sleeps with that being, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable One, if a monk is sleeping with an unordained person for more than two nights and during that time changes status by receiving full ordination as a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a nun is sleeping with an unordained person for more than two nights and during that time changes status by receiving full ordination as a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk sleeps together with an emanation for more than two nights in the same dwelling, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable One, if a monk sleeps with an unordained person for two nights, and then on the third night sleeps together with a paṇḍaka, what is the consequence?"
"It becomes both a downfall and a transgression."

"Venerable One, is there any case in which a monk might sleep in the same dwelling together with an unordained person without incurring an offense?"
"Upāli, there is. If it is a place where every side is uncovered, or surrounded by a fence, or half-surrounded, or not surrounded at all, or unenclosed, or half-unenclosed — if one sleeps in such a place, there is no offense."

"Venerable One, if a monk sleeps with an unordained person for more than two nights in a mountain cave, a hollow tree, or a dense thicket, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression."

"Venerable One, if one who has been given a training rule sleeps together with an unordained person for more than two nights, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a fully ordained nun sleeps together with an unordained person in the same dwelling for more than two nights, what is the consequence?"
"It is a transgression. For a female probationer, a novice nun, or male novices, it is a wrongdoing. The case of the monk Ariṣṭa, who was silenced three times and then declared to be in the remainder of the Saṅgha's judgment, applies here as well."

In brief:
By message, letter, gesture,
Or through another, from one to the next —
One who has become mad or mentally disturbed,
One who is ill or deaf — these are the categories.

Venerable Upāli asked the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable One, if the Blessed One has declared that a monk who, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in such a way and has not been followed in the Dharma, who has not abandoned the view of that wrongdoing, speaks with him, speaks with him repeatedly, seeks food from him, or sleeps together with him in the same dwelling — it becomes a transgression. Venerable One, if a monk who is seeking to speak with such a person as one who speaks in that way speaks by sending a message, or speaks repeatedly, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing. Likewise, sending a letter, using a gesture, having another convey the message, or passing it along from one to the next — all of these become wrongdoings."

"Venerable One, if a monk speaks with, speaks repeatedly with, seeks food from, or sleeps together in the same dwelling with a monk who is mad and has not been followed in the Dharma, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing. Likewise, one whose mind is disturbed, one afflicted by illness, one who is mute, one who is deaf, one who is simple-minded, or a monk who resides elsewhere and has not been followed in the Dharma — if one speaks with such a person, speaks repeatedly, eats with them, or sleeps together in the same dwelling, all of it becomes a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way and has not been followed in the Dharma, renders himself invisible by means of a mantra or a medicine, and then speaks with that person, speaks repeatedly, seeks food, or sleeps together with that person in the same dwelling, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

In brief:
Mantra, utterances of the sky,
Body, seclusion, and eating —
The seventh and the fourth are likewise —
And so too with the female and the neuter.

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way and has not been followed in the Dharma, renders himself invisible by means of a mantra or a medicine, and then speaks with that person, speaks repeatedly, seeks food, and sleeps together with that person in the same dwelling, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with such a person, they both go up into the sky and sleep there, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a noble one who is a monk addresses such a person who speaks in that way using the noble language, and that person does not respond in the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a noble one addresses that person who speaks in that way and has not been followed in the Dharma using a border language, and that person does not respond in a border language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if one who speaks a border language addresses such a person who speaks in that way using a border language, and that person does not respond in a border language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if one who speaks a border language addresses such a person who speaks in that way using the noble language, and that person does not respond in the noble language, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with such a person, makes himself understood through bodily signs, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, perceiving a secluded place as not secluded, speaks with or sleeps near such a person who speaks in that way, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way, shares a meal together with that person, and beyond that meal also shares other provisions —"

drinks, lickables, and tastables, and the like — what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way while still not yet fully ordained, speaks to that person while both are not yet fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk seeks that person out while not yet fully ordained, and speaks to them at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk seeks that person out while not yet fully ordained, and speaks to them after full ordination has been completed, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk seeks that person out at the moment of full ordination and speaks to them at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk seeks that person out at the moment of full ordination and speaks to them after full ordination has been completed, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk seeks that person out after full ordination has been completed and speaks to them after full ordination has been completed, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If the monk seeks that person out after full ordination has been completed and speaks to them while not yet fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk speaks to a person who speaks in that way, perceiving a fully ordained person as fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If the monk speaks to a fully ordained person, perceiving that person as not fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk speaks to a person who is not fully ordained, perceiving that person as fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk speaks to a person who is not fully ordained, perceiving that person as not fully ordained, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way, speaks to one who has not been consented to, perceiving that person as not consented to, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If the monk speaks to one who has not been consented to, perceiving that person as consented to, what is the consequence?"
"There is no offense."

"If the monk speaks to one who has been consented to, perceiving that person as not consented to, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"If the monk speaks to one who has been consented to, perceiving that person as consented to, what is the consequence?"
"There is no offense."

"Venerable One, if a monk speaks with a person who speaks in that way and in the course of speaking that person changes sex and becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a nun, while seeking to speak with a nun who speaks in that way, speaks with that nun and in the course of speaking that person changes sex and becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way, speaks with a pandaka, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Likewise, if the monk speaks with a nun who has been expelled, one who has killed his father, one who has killed his mother, one who has killed an arhat, one who has drawn blood from a Tathāgata with malicious intent, a tīrthika, one who has gone over to the tīrthikas, one who abides as a thief, one who does not abide in good standing, one who abides in a separate station, one who has previously caused a schism, or persons against whom a prior offense has arisen — in all such cases it is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk, while seeking to speak in that way with such a person, speaks with one who has caused a schism in the Saṅgha, one who has taken sides, or one to whom a training has been administered, what is the consequence?"
"In all cases it is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk speaks with a person who speaks in that way while that person is asleep, delirious, or intoxicated, and has not conformed to the Dharma, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if a monk speaks with a nun who speaks in that way, a female probationer, a female novice, or male novices, what is the consequence?"
"It is a wrongdoing."

"Venerable One, if one to whom a training has been administered, while seeking to speak with a person who speaks in that way and has not conformed to the Dharma, speaks with that person, speaks constantly with that person, seeks food together with that person, or sleeps near that person, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a nun, while seeking to speak with a nun who speaks in that way, speaks with that nun, speaks constantly with her, or sleeps together with her in the same dwelling, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, a nun and —"

"Venerable One, if one speaks with a novice monk who speaks in that way and has not conformed to the Dharma, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"With a probationer nun, a novice nun, and novice monks — it is a downfall. Just as with a person who speaks in that way, one must also declare that such a person has been shown to be unfit as a renunciant. When asked what the difference is, one must also explain the matter of service and veneration apart from work and provisions."

In brief:
The unfit, the marks, and so forth —
the fourth and the seventh are as stated —
all prohibitions, their nature,
the dyes, the training, and the nuns.

The venerable Upāli addressed the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable One, the Blessed One has declared that when a monk obtains a robe, he must discolor it by one of three means of discoloring; if he distributes a robe without having discolored it by any one of those three means, it becomes a downfall. Venerable One, is there a case where a monk distributes a robe without having discolored it by any one of the three means of discoloring, yet it does not become a downfall?"

"Upāli, there is: the use of a prohibited robe. A prohibited robe is one made of she-camel's wool, ox wool, goat's wool, wild animal's wool, a mixture of these, or cloth that has not been woven. If such a robe is used, it becomes an offense."

"Venerable One, if a monk uses a robe without having discolored it by any one of the three means of discoloring, and in the meantime his status changes and he becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a nun uses a robe without having discolored it by any one of the three means of discoloring, and in the meantime her status changes and she becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk perceives a robe that has been properly discolored as not having been discolored, and uses it, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If one perceives a robe that has not been discolored as having been discolored, and uses it, there is no offense."

"If one perceives a robe that has been discolored as not having been discolored, and uses it, what is the consequence?"
"It is an offense."

"If one perceives a robe that has been discolored as having been discolored, and uses it, what is the consequence?"
"There is no offense."

"Venerable One, if a robe was obtained before full ordination and one of the three means of discoloring was applicable to it, and one uses it without having discolored it after full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is an offense."

"If a robe was obtained before full ordination and one uses it as if still before full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is an offense."

"If a robe was obtained before full ordination and one uses it after having received full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a robe was obtained at the time of full ordination and one uses it at the time of full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is an offense."

"If a robe was obtained at the time of full ordination and one uses it after full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a robe was obtained after full ordination and one uses it after full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"If a robe was obtained after full ordination and one uses it without full ordination, what is the consequence?"
"It is an offense."

"Venerable One, if a monk uses a robe smaller than one cubit, or a piece of cloth the size of the Sugata's Dharma robe, without having discolored it by any one of the three means, what is the consequence?"
"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, is there a case where a monk uses a robe that has been discolored by one of the three means of discoloring, yet it nonetheless constitutes an offense?"

"Upāli, there is: when a monk uses a robe that is entirely blue, entirely yellow, or entirely red."

"Venerable One, is there a case where a monk uses a robe without having discolored it by any one of the three means of discoloring, and yet it does not constitute an offense?"

"Upāli, there is: namely, when that monk has divided up the cloth that is the nature of a robe."

"Venerable One, is there a case where a monk uses a robe that has been discolored by one of the three means of discoloring, and yet it nonetheless constitutes an offense?"

"Upāli, there is: when it has been dyed with a major dye. The major dyes are saffron, yellow orpiment, lac, madder, heartwood of the ra tree, and similar substances. If one uses a robe dyed with such dyes, it becomes a transgression."

"Venerable One, if one who has received the training uses a robe not discolored by any one of the three means of discoloring, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a nun uses a robe not discolored by any one of the three means of discoloring, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if female probationers, novice nuns, and male novices use a robe not discolored by any one of the three means of discoloring, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

In summary:
The rule on women and precious things is likewise so.
The fourth, on touching, is the same.
The rule for others, and the seventh, illustrates this.
Musical instruments and magical creations — bear this in mind.

The venerable Upāli then questioned the Blessed One, the Buddha: "Venerable One, the Blessed One has said that if a monk takes up with his own hand, or causes another to take up, a precious thing or something counted as precious, it becomes a downfall — except when he is within a boundary enclosure or within a residence. Venerable One, is there a case where a monk takes up with his own hand a precious thing or something counted as precious, and yet the offense does not become a downfall?"

"Upāli, there is: if one takes up one of the five precious things such as a precious woman and so forth, it is an offense proportionate to the actual act. However, if one takes up a precious jewel or a precious wheel, it is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk takes up a precious thing or something counted as precious, and then undergoes a change of sex and becomes a nun, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a nun takes up a precious thing or something counted as precious, and then undergoes a change of sex and becomes a monk, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk takes up a precious thing perceiving it as precious, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"If one takes up a precious thing perceiving it as not precious, what is the consequence?"

"There is no offense."

"If one takes up something that is not precious perceiving it as precious, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one takes up something that is not precious perceiving it as not precious, what is the consequence?"

"There is no offense."

"Likewise, perceiving something as being counted as precious is also to be applied in these four ways."

"Venerable One, if a monk hands over a precious thing or something counted as precious to another, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if a monk causes another to take up a precious thing or something counted as precious, what is the consequence?"

"It is a downfall."

"Venerable One, if, before full ordination, one sets out a precious thing or something counted as precious intending to take it, and takes it before full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one sets it out before full ordination and takes it at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one sets it out before full ordination and takes it after full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one sets it out at the moment of full ordination and takes it at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one sets it out at the moment of full ordination and takes it after full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one sets it out at the moment of full ordination and takes it at the moment of full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"If one sets it out at the moment of full ordination and takes it before full ordination, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrong deed."

"Venerable one, is there a case in which a monk may take a precious object or something equivalent to a precious object and yet not incur a transgression through a downfall?"

"Upāli, there is. If one takes a divine precious object or something equivalent to a precious object, it becomes a wrong deed."

"Venerable one, is there a case in which a monk may take something equivalent to a precious object and yet not incur a transgression through a downfall?"

"Upāli, there is. It is a case of taking something that is damaged."

"Venerable one, if a monk takes an emanated precious object or something equivalent to a precious object, what is the consequence?"

"It is a wrong deed."

"Venerable one, is there a case in which a monk may use a precious object or something equivalent to a precious object and yet not incur a transgression through a downfall?"

"Upāli, there is: in a dwelling place of gods, or a dwelling place of nāgas, or a dwelling place of yakṣas, or in a royal palace, or in the residence of a great minister of the king, where no seat or other receptacle is available."

"Venerable one, if one to whom a training has been given takes a precious object or something equivalent to a precious object, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."

"Venerable one, if a nun takes a precious object or something equivalent to a precious object, what is the consequence?"

"It is a transgression."
